guard_streams.source: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q4 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: Provider complaint rates and complaint drivers are service-quality indicators and cannot establish fixed-broadband coverage or parcel speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q4 2025 complaints update on 11 May 2026.
The figures cover October to December 2025.
Overall complaints increased from the previous quarter for the first time since 2023.
Broadband and landline complaints decreased while pay-TV complaints were unchanged.
TalkTalk and Vodafone generated the most broadband complaints.
Plusnet and Virgin Media generated the fewest broadband complaints.
O2 generated the most mobile complaints.
EE generated the most pay-TV complaints.
Ofcom identified unexpected mid-contract mobile price-rise announcements as a main complaint driver.
Ofcom publishes the figures to understand dissatisfaction and help comparisons, not to decide individual complaints.

guard_streams.source: Enforcement programme: industry's failure to implement One Touch Switch
guard_streams.write_limit: Switching-process enforcement and provider matching performance do not verify network coverage, postcode availability or parcel-measured speed.

facts.detail: The enforcement programme opened on 3 April 2023 and closed on 11 June 2026.
Fixed broadband and landline providers were required to implement One Touch Switch by 3 April 2023.
The regulatory requirements are in General Conditions C7.18 to C7.27.
Under OTS, the gaining provider organises the customer's switch.
OTS launched successfully for most customers on 12 September 2024.
Ofcom issued a formal information request in January 2025 about provider matching-rate issues.
Ofcom concluded that the majority of customers were successfully switching through OTS.
Ofcom became satisfied that providers had stopped using an alternative method after repeated OTS match failures.
The rules require a single residential switching process provided free of charge.
Ofcom states that easier switching supports competition and take-up of faster and more reliable broadband.
